nodes.name: pH-triggered W-Co hydroxide synthesis
nodes.procedure: Phosphotungstic acid (H3PW12O40) was first dissolved in water, resulting in monodisperse [PW12O40]³⁻ clusters with a Keggin structure. Co nitrite was introduced to supply Co cations, and the mixed solution was heated to 80°C. NH3·H2O was then added to raise the pH. This pH increase induced the decomposition of [PW12O40]³⁻ clusters into tetrahedral WO4²⁻ anions while simultaneously promoting the nucleation of α-phase Co(OH)x hydroxides with abundant oxygen vacancies. The negatively charged WO4²⁻ anions are adsorbed onto the positively charged α-Co(OH)x layers through electrostatic interaction, suppressing phase transition to β-Co(OH)2 and stabilizing the ultrathin structure.

nodes.procedure: W-Co(OH)x was then topologically converted into W-Co3O4 nanosheets by annealing in air at 450°C. W-Co3O4 retained the ultrathin morphology with high-density, non-aggregated W atoms and high BET surface area.

nodes.description: OER LSV performance in 1 M KOH
nodes.source_text: The OER electrocatalytic activity of W-Co₃O₄ in 1M KOH was measured using a glassy carbon electrode. nodes.description: Zn-air battery OER performance and stability
nodes.source_text: We then assembled zinc-air batteries (ZABs) using W-Co₃O₄ loaded on carbon paper as the air cathode... W-Co₃O₄ ZABs exhibit a charging voltage of 1.89V at a current density of 1mA cm⁻² and have a slight increase in voltage to 1.98V when the current is gradually increased to 20mA cm⁻²... The specific discharge capacity of W-Co₃O₄ ZABs was calculated to be 781mAh g⁻¹... the W-Co₃O₄ ZAB showed an excellent charge/discharge durability of 120 cycles.

nodes.description: AEMWE OER performance and stability at 60°C
nodes.source_text: Figure 7d presents the polarization curves of the W-Co₃O₄ catalyst in the AEMWE at 50°C. As an anodic catalyst, W-Co₃O₄ achieved current densities of 1000 and 3000mA cm⁻² at applied voltages of 2.12 and 2.45V, respectively. The AEMWE operates continuously at a current density of 200mA cm⁻² for over 100h.

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected HAADF-STEM reveals high-density and highly dispersed W single atoms in W-Co(OH)x with no W-containing clusters or nanoparticles observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) reveals the presence of high-density and highly dispersed W single atoms (Figure 2a,b), and no W-containing clusters or nanoparticles were observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: BET surface areas: W-Co(OH)x 118.5 m²/g (5.7× α-Co(OH)x at 20.8 m²/g), W-Co3O4 144.8 m²/g (5.7× Co3O4 from α-Co(OH)x, 7.5× from β-Co(OH)2 at 33.0 m²/g).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) specific surface area of W-Co(OH)x was measured at 118.5 m² g⁻¹, about 5.7 times higher than that of α-Co(OH)x (20.8 m² g⁻¹) and 3.7 times higher than that of β-Co(OH)2 (33.0 m² g⁻¹) (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of W-Co3O4 match spinel Co3O4 (PDF #42-1467) with diffraction peaks shifted to lower angles compared to pure Co3O4, confirming W doping and lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of W-Co3O4 were ascribed to spinel Co3O4 (PDF #42-1467) (Figure 2f), with very weak diffractions indicating the ultrathin structure. No W-containing phases were observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution EDS mapping shows Co, O, and W uniformly distributed at atomic level in W-Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution EDS mapping (Figure 2g) showed that Co, O, and W are uniformly distributed at the atomic level.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT k³-weighted EXAFS of W-Co3O4 shows single peak at 1.35 Å corresponding to W-O bond, confirming single-atom state of W.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Fourier transform (FT) k³-weighted extended X-ray absorption fine structures (EXAFS) spectra of W-Co3O4, only one main peak was observed at 1.35 Å, which corresponds to the W-O bond.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS shows right-shifted Co 2p peaks in W-Co3O4 indicating higher Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio and decreased Co valence state compared to pure Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For our W-Co3O4, the right-shifted Co 2p peaks indicate a higher Co²⁺/Co³⁺ ratio, suggesting a decrease in Co valence state.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV determines electrochemical double-layer capacitance Cdl of 2.17 mF/cm² for W-Co3O4 and 0.40 mF/cm² for Co3O4.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The slope of the change in current (Δj) at a specific potential against the scan rate was twice the Cdl, allowing the determination of Cdl values for W-Co3O4 and Co3O4 as 2.17 and 0.40 mF cm⁻² respectively (Figure 3d).

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows charge transfer resistance Rct of 16.5 Ω for W-Co3O4, much lower than 85.4 Ω for Co3O4 and 96.9 Ω for IrO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By fitting the Nyquist plots with an equivalent circuit, the charge transfer resistance (Rct) of W-Co3O4 was determined to be 16.5 Ω, much lower than those of Co3O4 (85.4 Ω) and IrO2 (96.9 Ω).
